body.estimand_functional: \(\tau(z_0)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\{\mathbb E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0]-m_s(z_{0s})\},\quad \operatorname{MSE}(\widehat\tau)\asymp R_{\star}\text{ conditional on event-date transport and the attainable-direction restriction}\)

sampling_model.design: For each fixed cohort, \(T\) exact pre-event proxy paths are drawn from a density bounded above and away from zero on \([0,1]^d\); the theorem first conditions on their realized local-polynomial geometry.
sampling_model.units: Each cohort supplies \(n_s\) replicated untreated wealth blocks per pre-event window and \(n_s\) treated event wealth levels; histories are conditionally independent across units and geometrically beta-mixing across calendar windows.
sampling_model.treatment: A cohort enters the event path once. Consistency links observed event wealth to treated potential wealth, and the explicitly maintained event-date transport equality supplies the untreated conditional mean. The observed design cannot test that cross-date counterfactual equality.
sampling_model.overlap: Every realized cohort path is at least \(\delta_0\) from the boundary of \([0,1]^d\), and the training density is at least \(c_X\) there.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The event path is the mean of \(N\) donor scores with unknown full covariance \(\Sigma\). Every foldwise donor mean is projected coordinatewise onto \(([0,1]^d)^S\), covariance eigenvalues are clipped to \([c_\Sigma/2,2C_\Sigma]\), and a deterministic finite dyadic bandwidth search has a clipped pooled-response fallback. Separated calendar blocks use fixed gap and block sequences; training coordinates are exactly observed, so donor noise moves only the evaluation center.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 7 gives the fixed-point local-polynomial squared-risk rate, and Theorem 8 evaluates that estimator at an independent estimated minimizer under strong convexity.
Theorem 1 expands a local-linear regression estimator when an estimated covariate is attached to every training observation.
Theorems 3.1--3.6 recover known-error deconvolution performance when every latent training coordinate is observed with replicated classical error.
The optimal finite-\(q\) norm rate for a derivative of order \(m\) of a \(p\)-smooth \(d\)-dimensional regression is \(n^{-(p-m)/(2p+d)}\).
Local-linear smoothers attain the ordinary pointwise minimax order and high asymptotic minimax efficiency under fixed or random design.
Ordered moduli yield finite-sample optimal confidence intervals for linear functionals over convex regression classes in a known Gaussian experiment.
Bias-aware local-polynomial intervals have uniform asymptotic coverage and near-optimal length when a centered uniform limit and worst-case bias bound are available.
Synthetic-control prediction intervals account for weight-estimation and post-treatment innovation uncertainty, with a beta-mixing extension based on block coupling.
Proposition 3.1 gives synthetic-control factor-loading recovery and weight dilution when controls and pre-treatment periods jointly grow.

body.tldr: The causal target is cohort-weighted buy-and-hold level wealth at a fixed realized event path, identified by consistency and an explicitly untestable event-date counterfactual transport equality. Historical proxy paths are observed exactly, whereas the event path alone is generated from an independent donor sample with unknown full covariance. This sigma-field distinction converts donor uncertainty into a covariance-standardized Holder location modulus rather than a deconvolution operator. Conditional on a disclosed one-direction lower-modulus condition, the kernel is a conditional minimax theorem over realized local-polynomial geometry, an explicit four-channel marginal phase diagram across arbitrary donor, calendar, and replication growth, and a matching uniformly honest expected-length frontier. Projected donor centers, a deterministic finite bandwidth grid, clipped fits, and a full-range bad-sample interval make both procedures samplewise total. A bounded non-affine worked DGP establishes non-vacuity of the maintained direction; exact constants at phase intersections remain open.

project_justification.gap: Classical nonparametric regression fixes the evaluation point, generated-regressor expansions perturb every training coordinate, and measurement-error regression convolves every latent training coordinate. Synthetic-control inference likewise does not separate replicated smoothing, random spacing, and an external nonregular donor center in one causal experiment.
project_justification.niche: Event studies often record historical market paths directly but synthesize only the event-date untreated path from donors. With many units per calendar window, response noise can vanish faster than the spatial resolution of the finite set of historical paths, exposing a spacing phase that ordinary one-observation-per-site asymptotics suppress.
project_justification.fill: The project separates the pre-event regression from the untestable event-date transport premise, states the observation sigma-fields, conditions first on realized Gram geometry, and derives the maximum of treated noise, replicated smoothing, spacing, and covariance-standardized donor uncertainty conditional on a disclosed attainable direction. It constructs a samplewise total cross-fitted estimator using projected fold centers, a finite first-coercive bandwidth rule, clipped fits, and a pooled-mean fallback. Its explicit block interval uses centered influence-score block variance, treated-mean variance, a fourth-moment donor radius, spectral covariance clipping, and a conservative full-range value on every bad sample. Matching estimation and expected-length lower bounds remain in the same causal class, and a bounded non-affine DGP demonstrates that the direction condition is non-vacuous.

body.related_work: Stone (1982), Fan (1993), and Fan et al. (1997) provide the ordinary Holder and local-polynomial benchmark, including multivariate Gram and minimax calculations, but have neither site replication nor a generated query. Gaiffas (2007) establishes spatially normalized global sup-risk under inhomogeneous random design; its logarithm belongs to uniform spatial loss and does not settle the realized-point spacing term here. Mammen, Rothe, and Schienle (2012) derive a differentiable stochastic expansion when generated coordinates enter every training row. Hahn and Ridder (2013) derive pathwise influence corrections for smooth generated regressors. Delaigle, Hall, and Meister (2008) and Fan and Truong (1993) study the different experiment in which every training coordinate is classically contaminated and Fourier inversion is required. Akhavan, Gogolashvili, and Tsybakov (2024) is the closest clean-training random-center construction: its Theorems 7 and 8 sample-split an estimated minimizer from a regularized local-polynomial evaluation, but strong convexity makes center error second order and removes a separate external \(N^{-\kappa}\) phase. Donoho (1994), Low (1997), and Armstrong and Kolesar (2018, 2020) supply modulus and bias-aware honest-inference machinery for fixed Gaussian or ordinary regression experiments. Ferman (2021) organizes simultaneous donor and period growth through factor recovery. Cattaneo, Feng, and Titiunik (2021) supply a full-covariance dependent synthetic-control prediction template, while Chernozhukov, Wuthrich, and Zhu (2021) already occupy the conformal block-permutation route. Abadie (2021) and Arkhangelsky and Imbens (2024) locate the result within synthetic-control and causal-panel practice.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The no-deconvolution conclusion is conditional on the exact observation structure. If an estimated proxy map is applied to every pre-event row, the Mammen--Rothe--Schienle generated-regressor expansion becomes relevant; if only noisy replicates of every latent training coordinate are observed, the Delaigle--Hall--Meister deconvolution experiment applies. Cross-fitting alone does not convert either design into a generated-center experiment. The pointwise spacing term is \(T^{-2\lambda/d}\); uniform coverage over every path in the cube would generally replace it by a logarithmically inflated global fill-distance term. Totalization does not permit exceptional samples to be ignored: the upper-bound and expected-length proofs must bound the probability of every bandwidth fallback, inadequate block count, and undefined raw variance denominator, including the full-range interval's contribution. The worked law \(P_{\mathrm{ex}}\) establishes only that the attainable-direction restriction is non-vacuous; it does not derive that restriction for the general panel class.
body.honest_scope: The event-date transport equality is a maintained cross-date counterfactual restriction that the observed design cannot test. Rolling untreated pseudo-events can diagnose or falsify stability within the pre-event period, but cannot verify transport to the untreated event date; an institutional stability story is motivation rather than evidence. The \(N^{-\kappa}\) MSE converse and the \(N^{-\kappa/2}\) expected-length converse are conditional on \texttt{ass:attainable-local-modulus}, so Theorems 1--3 and the proposal are capped at field tier. The effective dimension is \(d=p(H+1)\) because the stacked path is unrestricted; a \(d=p\) claim would require an additional shared-index structure and is not made. The scalar \(H=0\), \(S=p=d=1\), and \(0<\lambda\le1\) reduction is explicit in Theorem 2. Exact minimax constants, automatic smoothness adaptation, growing path dimension, and uniform-in-path bands remain open.
